title: The False Prophet
lead: A false prophet is one who speaks in the LORD's name without being sent by him, or who speaks for other gods, or whose word does not come true (Deuteronomy 13:1–5; 18:20–22). Jeremiah and Ezekiel fought such prophets in Jerusalem (Jeremiah 23; 28; Ezekiel 13), and Jesus warned of false prophets who come with signs and wonders (Matthew 7:15; Matthew 24:24). "The false prophet" is also Revelation's name for the beast from the earth, which has horns like a lamb and talks like a dragon and makes the world worship the first beast (Revelation 13:11–17; Revelation 16:13; Revelation 19:20). For the wider question of false teaching, see "False Teachers and False Prophets."

sections.b: The Law gives three tests: the prophet was not sent, or speaks for other gods even when a sign comes true, or the word does not happen (Deuteronomy 13:1–5; 18:20–22). Jeremiah adds that false prophets speak from their own hearts and say "peace" when there is no peace (Jeremiah 23:9–40; 28–29). Ezekiel adds more: false visions will end (12:24); the prophets follow their own spirit and do not repair the breaches in the wall, but cover it with whitewash (13:1–23; the same picture lies behind Paul's words to the high priest in Acts 23:3); they are paid in handfuls of barley and pieces of bread (13:19); and a prophet who is deceived is guilty with the one who asked him (14:9–10). Later Jewish law gave the false prophet his own rules (Mishnah Sanhedrin 11:5). Jesus tests prophets by their fruit and predicts many (Matthew 7:15–23; 24:11, 24), and 2 Peter 2:1 warns of false teachers who will rise among believers as false prophets once did among Israel.

sections.b: In Revelation 13:11–17 the figure is a second beast, from the land, who works signs, speaks for the first beast and enforces its worship. Later in the book the same figure is called "the false prophet" (Revelation 16:13; 19:20; 20:10). Read against the whole Bible, he is one case of the pattern above: a prophet whose power is borrowed and whose message leads people from God.
